public_rationale: Skywork released its own OR1 models and explicitly identified DeepSeek-R1-Distill models as their starting points. That satisfies the forecast's derivative-model branch. Because the statement uses 'or', proving independent cloud deployment as well is unnecessary. This finding establishes reuse, not the size of its commercial effect on DeepSeek.
limitations: The derivative starts from DeepSeek's distilled Qwen models rather than the full R1 model.
The evidence does not quantify adoption or DeepSeek's lost revenue.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Others will build their own models from DeepSeek's work or run their own DeepSeek instances on rented cloud GPUs.

statement.excerpt: Whether or not someone chooses to pay DeepSeek is largely irrelevant — someone else will take what it’s created and build their own, or people will start running their own DeepSeek instances renting GPUs from one of the various cloud computing firms.

from_speaker: someone else will take what it’s created and build their own
or people will start running their own DeepSeek instances
our_interpretation: The forecast is disjunctive: an actual third-party derivative model or an actual independent deployment on rented cloud GPUs suffices.
Building on DeepSeek includes further training a released DeepSeek model, including a distilled model. It does not require reproducing the original model from scratch.
The opening statement about paying DeepSeek describes technical independence from its hosted service, not a quantified prediction about DeepSeek revenue.
criteria.support_condition: After the post, a third party publicly releases an identifiable model derived from DeepSeek's work, or documents an actual independent DeepSeek deployment on rented cloud GPUs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event permanently rules out both third-party derivatives and independent cloud deployment. Mere non-occurrence over a finite interval is insufficient.
